# 🎓 BharatMentor

**Voice-first Multilingual AI Learning Mentor — English, Hindi & Hinglish**

> Built as proof-of-work for an AI/ML Applied Engineer / Voice-first AI internship,
> specifically to demonstrate voice AI, multilingual interaction, RAG quality,
> and reproducible evaluation.

---

## Why BharatMentor?

Most AI tutoring systems are text-first English-only chatbots.
Indian students often think and speak in Hindi, Hinglish, or their mother tongue — not formal English.

BharatMentor focuses on:
1. **Voice-first interaction** — speak your question, hear the answer
2. **Multilingual** — English, Hindi, Hinglish supported
3. **Grounded answers** — RAG over course material, source-cited
4. **Measured quality** — WER, Recall@5, MRR, conversation evaluation

---

## Architecture

```
Streamlit UI
     │
     ▼
FastAPI (app/main.py)
     │
     ▼
Agent Loop (app/agent.py)
  ├── search_knowledge()   → RAG retrieval
  ├── get_student_progress() → SQLite/PostgreSQL
  ├── generate_quiz()      → LLM-generated JSON quiz
  └── calculator()         → Safe AST evaluator (no eval())
     │
     ▼
LLM Provider (Groq | Gemini) — configurable via .env

Voice Pipeline:
  Audio → faster-whisper STT → Agent → gTTS TTS → Audio
```

See [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) for detailed diagrams.

---

## Agent Workflow

```
Student speaks
      ↓ faster-whisper (base model, CPU, int8)
Transcript + language detection
      ↓
Agent (max 5 tool rounds)
      ↓ tool selected
Tool executes (RAG / DB / calculator / quiz)
      ↓
LLM synthesises answer with source citations
      ↓ gTTS
Audio response
```

---

## RAG Methodology

- **Corpus:** 2–3 educational PDFs (Physics — Mechanics)
- **Chunking:** ~400 char overlapping chunks, preserving document/page/section
- **Embeddings:** `sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` (384-dim)
- **Retrieval:** vectorised cosine similarity
- **Fallback:** TF-IDF when index not built

Each answer includes source citations:
```
Sources:
  mechanics — Page 14
  mechanics — Page 16
```

---

## Evaluation

### RAG Evaluation

| Metric | Value | Target |
|--------|-------|--------|
| Recall@1 | **86.67%** | > 80% |
| Recall@3 | **100.0%** | > 90% |
| Recall@5 | **100.0%** | > 95% |
| MRR | **92.22%** | > 85% |

Dataset: 15 in-domain + 2 out-of-domain verified questions on Mechanics.
See [`experiments/rag/`](experiments/rag/).

### ASR Evaluation (English Baseline)

| Metric | Measured Value |
|--------|----------------|
| STT Engine | faster-whisper (`base`, CPU, `int8`) |
| Average RTF (Real-Time Factor) | **0.54** (2.3s audio in ~1.2s) |
| English Transcription Accuracy | **100%** on target queries |
| TTS Engine | gTTS (`GTTSProvider`, MP3) |

See [`experiments/asr/`](experiments/asr/).

### Conversation Evaluation

10 representative conversations evaluated on:
- Relevance, Correctness, Groundedness, Conciseness (LLM-judge, 1–5)
- Language consistency (deterministic check)

> ⚠️ LLM-judge scores are approximate. See [`docs/limitations.md`](docs/limitations.md).

---

## Setup

### 1. Clone and install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yourhandle/bharatmentor
cd bharatmentor
python -m venv .venv
# Windows:
.venv\Scripts\activate
# Linux/Mac:
source .venv/bin/activate

pip install -r requirements.txt
```

### 2. Configure

```bash
cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env: set GROQ_API_KEY (or GEMINI_API_KEY)
```

### 3. Seed database

```bash
python seed.py
```

### 4. Run tests

```bash
pytest tests/ -v
```

### 5. Start API

```bash
uvicorn app.main:app --reload
# API at http://localhost:8000
# Docs at http://localhost:8000/docs
```

### 6. Start Streamlit UI

```bash
streamlit run frontend/streamlit_app.py
```

---

## Build RAG Index

Place 1–2 Physics PDFs in `data/knowledge/`:
```bash
python -m rag.ingestion
```

Run evaluation:
```bash
python -m rag.evaluation
```

---

## Run Voice Pipeline Tests

```bash
# Requires audio samples in experiments/asr/dataset/en/ and /hi/
python experiments/asr/evaluate.py
```

---

## Project Structure

```
bharatmentor/
├── app/
│   ├── agent.py          # Agent loop
│   ├── tools.py          # Four tools
│   ├── db.py             # SQLAlchemy models
│   ├── llm.py            # LLM provider abstraction
│   ├── config.py         # pydantic-settings config
│   └── main.py           # FastAPI app
├── voice/
│   ├── stt.py            # faster-whisper STT
│   ├── tts.py            # gTTS TTS
│   └── pipeline.py       # Voice pipeline
├── rag/
│   ├── ingestion.py      # PDF → chunks → embeddings
│   ├── retrieval.py      # Cosine similarity retrieval
│   └── evaluation.py     # Recall@5, MRR
├── evaluation/
│   └── conversation_eval.py
├── frontend/
│   └── streamlit_app.py
├── experiments/
│   ├── rag/              # dataset.json, results.json, report.md
│   ├── asr/              # evaluate.py, dataset/, results.json
│   └── conversation/     # cases.json, results.json
├── tests/
│   ├── conftest.py       # Fixtures + mock LLMs
│   ├── test_tools.py
│   ├── test_db.py
│   ├── test_api.py
│   └── test_agent.py
├── docs/
│   ├── architecture.md
│   ├── limitations.md
│   └── progress.md
├── data/
│   ├── knowledge/        # Place PDFs here
│   └── index/            # Generated: chunks.json + embeddings.npy
```

---

## LLM Provider

Configurable via `.env`:

```env
LLM_PROVIDER=groq   # or gemini
GROQ_API_KEY=...
```

Groq free tier: https://console.groq.com
Gemini free tier: https://aistudio.google.com

---

## Limitations

See [`docs/limitations.md`](docs/limitations.md) for honest assessment of:
- gTTS internet requirement
- faster-whisper Hindi accuracy on CPU
- Hinglish ASR challenges
- LLM-as-judge reliability

---

## Related Work

**AgencyOS** (separate project) demonstrates:
- Multi-agent orchestration
- Redis + Docker infrastructure
- Complex API workflows
- Production auth

BharatMentor focuses specifically on voice AI and measurable evaluation quality.

readme:
# Beep Product Execution Copilot

An AI-powered Product Management execution copilot that transforms informal product prototypes into structured PRDs, computes transparent version diffs, enforces deliberate human approval, and deterministically generates dependency-aware engineering ticket backlogs and timelines.

---

## Why I Built This

The product-to-engineering handoff is notoriously friction-heavy in modern software teams. Prototype revisions, informal Slack discussions, and iterative scope changes often lead to stale documentation, silent feature creep, untracked dependencies, and inaccurate sprint schedules. 

Product Managers spend hours manually translating feature descriptions into standardized PRDs, documenting what changed between iterations, breaking down requirements into Jira/Linear tickets, and attempting to map out dependency sequences.

**Beep Product Execution Copilot** bridges this gap:
1. It eliminates blank-page syndrome by converting raw product prototype notes into clean, standardized 7-section PRDs.
2. It makes iterative scope changes completely visible through deterministic, section-by-section diffs and changelogs.
3. It preserves engineering integrity by requiring explicit PM approval before tickets can be generated.
4. It decomposes approved requirements into story-pointed tickets and computes a mathematically deterministic timeline and dependency graph—preventing AI hallucination in scheduling.

---

## What It Does

The application implements a closed-loop execution workflow:

```text
Prototype Input
      ↓
Structured PRD Generation (AI)
      ↓
Version Diff & Changelog (Deterministic)
      ↓
Explicit PM Approval Gate (Human-in-the-Loop)
      ↓
Development Ticket Decomposition (AI)
      ↓
Dependency Validation & Cycle Detection (Deterministic)
      ↓
Topological Scheduling & Timeline (Deterministic)
      ↓
Artifact Exports (Markdown / JSON)
```

---

## Problem Statements Covered

This project delivers two core numbered problem statements:

1. **Problem Statement 7 (PS7) — Prototype → PRD Generator + Versioning + Diff**
   - Ingests raw product prototypes.
   - Generates structured 7-section PRDs.
   - Maintains append-only version history with immutable prototype snapshots.
   - Computes deterministic section-by-section diffs and changelogs between versions.
   - Provides explicit version approval.

2. **Problem Statement 10 (PS10) — Approved PRD → Development Tickets + Dependencies + Timeline**
   - Decomposes approved PRD requirements into story-pointed development tickets.
   - Supports **manually pasted valid PRD JSON** as an alternate input path (AC11).
   - Validates ticket structure and establishes traceability links back to source PRD sections.
   - Validates dependency integrity and detects circular dependencies.
   - Deterministically schedules start and due dates using Kahn's topological sort.
   - Renders interactive Backlog cards, SVG directed Dependency Graphs, and Gantt Timelines.
   - Exports PRDs, Changelogs, and Ticket Backlogs to Markdown and JSON.

---

## PS7 — Prototype to PRD

PS7 manages the definition and evolution of product requirements:

- **Structured 7-Section Schema:** Every generated PRD adheres to 7 standardized sections:
  1. `overview` (string)
  2. `goals` (string array)
  3. `nonGoals` (string array)
  4. `userStories` (string array)
  5. `functionalRequirements` (string array)
  6. `nonFunctionalRequirements` (string array)
  7. `openQuestions` (string array)
- **Append-Only Versioning:** Generating a new PRD never overwrites existing versions. Each iteration increments the version number (`v1`, `v2`, ...), preserving an immutable snapshot of the prototype text that created it.
- **Structured Section-by-Section Diff Engine:** Rather than performing loose text diffing on raw markdown, the custom TypeScript diff engine compares structured JSON fields:
  - Sentence-level diffing for narrative sections (`overview`).
  - Item exact-match and >50% Jaccard word-overlap similarity pairing for list sections to identify added, removed, and modified requirements.
- **Human-Readable Changelog:** Renders color-coded diff summaries (added in green, removed in red, modified in amber) showing exactly what changed between iterations.
- **Explicit Approval Gate:** All new PRD versions start in `draft` status. A PM must deliberately review and click **✓ Approve PRD** before downstream ticket generation is unlocked.

---

## PS10 — PRD to Development Plan

PS10 turns requirements into an actionable engineering delivery plan:

- **Approved PRD Gate:** Generating tickets from project PRDs requires an explicitly approved version (Rule C6).
- **Manual PRD JSON Input Path (AC11):** Evaluators or engineers can also paste an external PRD JSON directly into the ticket generation tab. The input is validated against the identical schema and converges into the exact same downstream pipeline.
- **Ticket Decomposition:** Gemini decomposes PRD requirements into engineering tickets with title, description, acceptance criteria, story points (Fibonacci-aligned estimates), dependency references (`dependsOn`), and source PRD section tags.
- **Strict Schema Validation:** Validates ticket responses, rejecting missing titles, invalid IDs, or malformed arrays before passing to the scheduler.
- **Source Section Traceability:** Each ticket retains a `sourceSection` badge (e.g. `functionalRequirements`). Clicking the badge automatically switches to the PRD view and highlights the corresponding PRD section with an animated outline.
- **Dependency Graph & Cycle Detection:** Builds an adjacency list, checks for invalid or self-referential IDs, and runs Kahn's algorithm. If a circular dependency is detected (e.g., `T-1 → T-2 → T-1`), it flags the cycle without crashing and surfaces an explanatory alert.
- **Interactive Views:**
  - **Backlog List:** Rich ticket cards displaying story points, calculated duration, scheduled dates, acceptance checklist, dependency chips, and traceability links.
  - **Dependency Graph:** Interactive SVG directed graph laying out tickets in topological columns with curved Bézier connection arrows.
  - **Gantt Timeline:** Visual bar chart plotting scheduled ticket durations against calendar days with project milestone badges.
- **Artifact Exporters:** Clean one-click exports for:
  - PRD (`.md`)
  - Version Changelog (`.md`)
  - Ticket Backlog (`.json`)
  - Development Backlog (`.md`)

---

## AI vs Deterministic Logic

A foundational architectural decision in PRD Pilot is strict separation between AI-powered creative synthesis and deterministic state transformations:

| Responsibility | Implementation | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| **Prototype → PRD Synthesis** | **AI** (`Google Gemini`) | Natural language understanding and domain synthesis are ideal for LLMs. |
| **PRD Schema Validation** | **Deterministic** (`validator.ts`) | Guarantees all 7 required sections exist and conform to types. |
| **PRD Versioning & Storage** | **Deterministic** (`projectStore.ts`) | Prevents accidental overwrites and ensures immutable history. |
| **Section-by-Section Diffing** | **Deterministic** (`diff.ts`) | Jaccard similarity and exact matching provide 100% predictable changelogs. |
| **PRD Approval State** | **Deterministic** (`projectStore.ts`) | Requires deliberate human authorization; AI cannot approve PRDs. |
| **PRD → Ticket Decomposition** | **AI** (`Google Gemini`) | Translates user stories and functional requirements into engineering tasks. |
| **Ticket Schema Validation** | **Deterministic** (`validator.ts`) | Rejects incomplete tickets or invalid schemas before execution. |
| **Dependency Validation & Cycle Detection** | **Deterministic** (`scheduler.ts`) | Kahn's algorithm mathematically guarantees graph validity and detects loops. |
| **Duration & Date Calculations** | **Deterministic** (`scheduler.ts`) | Eliminates AI hallucination in scheduling formulas and date arithmetic. |
| **Topological Sort & Tie-Breaking** | **Deterministic** (`scheduler.ts`) | Lexicographical ID sorting ensures 100% reproducible execution order. |
| **Markdown & JSON Export Generation** | **Deterministic** (`exporter.ts`) | Pure template formatting ensuring structured, valid files. |

---

## Scheduling Heuristic

The application enforces the **C2 Scheduling Rule** deterministically in pure TypeScript:

```text
duration_days = ceil(story_points / 10 × 14)

If ticket has no dependencies:
    start_date = project_start_date

If ticket has dependencies:
    start_date = latest_dependency_due_date + 1 calendar day

due_date = start_date + duration_days
```

### Explanation in Plain English
- **Velocity Assumption:** Assumes a standard team velocity heuristic of **10 story points per 14 calendar days** (2 weeks).
- **Duration Formula:** A 5 SP ticket requires `ceil((5 / 10) * 14) = 7` calendar days. An 8 SP ticket requires `ceil((8 / 10) * 14) = 12` calendar days.
- **Dependency Date Rule:** Independent tickets start immediately on the configurable `project_start_date`. Dependent tickets start on the **next calendar day** following the latest completion date among their prerequisite tickets.
- **Deterministic Date Math:** Dates are computed using UTC calendar day arithmetic (`addDays`, `getNextCalendarDay`).
- **Planning Heuristic Label:** *This is a planning heuristic for timeline modeling and dependency visualization—not a capacity-accurate engineering estimate.* AI does NOT generate ticket dates or durations.

---

## Key Product Decisions

1. **Human-in-the-Loop Approval Gate:** AI generates suggestions, but the PM retains governance. Ticket generation is strictly locked until a PRD version is reviewed and approved.
2. **AI Never Controls Schedules or Graph Topologies:** LLMs are prone to arithmetic errors and date hallucinations. The AI only suggests task breakdown and dependency IDs; all date math, cycle detection, and topological sorting are strictly deterministic.
3. **Append-Only Version History:** Requirement revisions create new versions rather than silently mutating existing ones. PRD version snapshots remain permanently auditable alongside the prototype text that prompted them.
4. **Structured JSON Diffing over Raw Text Diffing:** Diffing the validated structured PRD object eliminates whitespace/formatting noise from the LLM, producing clean, actionable changelogs.
5. **Bidirectional Traceability:** Every ticket links back to its origin PRD section (`functionalRequirements`, `userStories`, etc.), allowing engineers and PMs to trace *why* a ticket exists.
6. **Unified Dual-Input Pipeline:** Whether tickets are generated from an approved project PRD or from a manually pasted JSON PRD, both converge into the identical schema validation, decomposition, and scheduling engine.

---

## Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        UI Layer                        │
│  HomePage · PrototypePage · TicketsPage · ExportPanel  │
│  PrdViewer · ChangelogViewer · TicketCard · GanttChart │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            │
              ┌─────────────┴─────────────┐
              ▼                           ▼
   ┌────────────────────┐      ┌────────────────────┐
   │     LLM Layer      │      │  Pure Logic Layer  │
   │  client.ts         │      │  scheduler.ts      │
   │  prdPrompt.ts      │      │  diff.ts           │
   │  ticketPrompt.ts   │      │  exporter.ts       │
   └──────────┬─────────┘      └──────────▲─────────┘
              │                           │
              ▼                           │
   ┌────────────────────┐                 │
   │  Validator Layer   │                 │
   │  validator.ts      ├─────────────────┘
   └──────────┬─────────┘
              │
              ▼
   ┌────────────────────────────────┐
   │        Store / Session         │
   │  projectStore.ts (localStorage)│
   │  sessionStore.ts (in-memory)   │
   └────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Module Organization
- `src/config/`: Application and LLM model configuration (`llm.config.ts`).
- `src/data/`: Demo fixture data (`demoSeed.ts`).
- `src/llm/`: Gemini client wrapper, typed prompts, and strict JSON schema validators (`client.ts`, `validator.ts`, `prompts/`).
- `src/logic/`: Pure, deterministic TypeScript logic engines for scheduling (`scheduler.ts`), diffing (`diff.ts`), and exports (`exporter.ts`).
- `src/store/`: Persistence abstraction for projects in localStorage (`projectStore.ts`) and ephemeral in-memory session management (`sessionStore.ts`).
- `src/types/`: TypeScript interfaces and schemas for PRDs, diffs, and tickets (`prd.ts`, `ticket.ts`).
- `src/ui/`: Components, pages, and CSS design system (`components/`, `pages/`, `styles/main.css`).

---

## Data & Persistence

- **Project & PRD Storage:** Saved in browser `localStorage` under keys `prd_pilot_projects` and `prd_pilot_tickets`.
- **API Key Security:** The Google Gemini API key is stored **in-memory only** (`sessionStore.ts`) and is **never** written to `localStorage`, cookies, or session storage. Closing the browser tab or clicking clear immediately purges the key.
- **No Backend Database:** Built as a self-contained client-side single-page application.
- **No User Tracking or Authentication:** No login or backend session tracking required.

---

## Demo Walkthrough (Evaluator Guide)

To evaluate the complete end-to-end workflow:

1. **Open the App:** Navigate to the live URL or run locally on `http://localhost:5173`.
2. **Explore Pre-Seeded Demo:** Click **🎯 Load Demo Project** on the home screen. This loads the "Referral Rewards" demo project containing 2 draft PRD versions. *(No API key is needed to inspect pre-seeded data).*
3. **Inspect PRD v1 & v2:** In the **Prototype → PRD** tab, view the structured 7 sections of PRD v2.
4. **Review Changelog:** Scroll down to the **What Changed** card to see the structured diff between v1 and v2 (e.g. tier structure additions, fraud prevention rules, $20 → $30 threshold modification).
5. **Approve PRD:** Click **✓ Approve PRD v2**. Notice the status badge updates to `Approved`.
6. **Navigate to Tickets:** Click the **🎫 PRD → Tickets** tab.
7. **Enter Gemini API Key (Optional for Live Generation):** Enter your Gemini API key in the top banner. *(Requires Gemini 3.5 Flash / 2.0 access)*.
8. **Generate Development Backlog:** Click **🎫 Generate Backlog Tickets**.
9. **Inspect Views:**
   - **Backlog List:** Review story points, calculated dates, and acceptance criteria.
   - **Dependency Graph:** Switch to the graph tab to view topological columns and dependency flow.
   - **Gantt Timeline:** Switch to the Gantt chart to view the sequential calendar timeline.
10. **Test Traceability:** Click any ticket's source badge (`📌 Functional Requirements`) to jump back to the PRD view and highlight the linked section.
11. **Test Manual PRD Input (AC11):** Switch PRD input source to **📝 Paste PRD Manually (JSON)**, paste custom PRD JSON, click **✓ Validate PRD**, and generate tickets.
12. **Export Artifacts:** Use the **📥 Export Artifacts** panel to download PRDs, changelogs, JSON tickets, or Markdown backlogs.

---

## Running Locally

### Prerequisites
- Node.js (v18+ recommended)
- npm

### Installation & Execution Commands

```bash
# 1. Install dependencies
npm install

# 2. Start local Vite development server
npm run dev

# 3. Run all automated unit tests (Vitest)
npm test

# 4. Run TypeScript compilation check
npx tsc --noEmit

# 5. Build production bundle
npm run build

# 6. Preview production build locally
npm run preview
```

### Providing the Gemini API Key
- Enter your Gemini API key directly into the secure in-page banner at the top of the app.
- The key is held strictly in memory in JS closure and is never saved to disk or `.env`.

---

## Testing

The project has comprehensive automated unit test coverage across 5 dedicated test suites.

**Test Results:** **43 / 43 tests passing** (100% pass rate) | **0 TypeScript errors** (`npx tsc --noEmit`).

### Test Suites Breakdown
1. **`src/logic/manualPrd.test.ts` (4 tests):**
   - Valid manual PRD JSON schema acceptance.
   - Clean rejection of malformed or incomplete PRD JSON.
   - Manual PRD pipeline execution into the deterministic scheduler.
   - Parity and convergence between approved PRD and manual PRD scheduling outputs.
2. **`src/llm/validator.test.ts` (8 tests):**
   - 7-section PRD schema validation and non-empty string checks.
   - Rejection of invalid JSON syntax, non-objects, and missing sections.
   - Ticket array schema validation, title enforcement, and field type checking.
3. **`src/logic/scheduler.test.ts` (11 tests):**
   - Single ticket scheduling with no dependencies.
   - Linear 3-ticket dependency chains (`T-1 → T-2 → T-3`).
   - Branching dependency graphs (1 prerequisite, multiple dependents).
   - Independent parallel ticket tracks.
   - Multi-dependency convergence (dependent on multiple prerequisites).
   - Circular dependency detection without crashing (`T-1 ↔ T-2`).
   - Sanitization of non-existent or self-referential dependency IDs.
   - Deterministic tie-breaking by ticket ID for 100% reproducible ordering.
   - Strict C2 duration formula validation (`ceil(SP / 10 * 14)`).
   - Configurable project start dates.
4. **`src/logic/diff.test.ts` (16 tests):**
   - Unchanged item detection.
   - Added item detection.
   - Removed item detection.
   - Modified item detection using >50% Jaccard word similarity pairing.
   - Immutability of previous PRD versions during diffing.
   - Multi-section diff aggregations.
5. **`src/logic/exporter.test.ts` (4 tests):**
   - PRD to Markdown export formatting with all 7 sections and metadata.
   - Changelog to Markdown export with added/removed/modified tags.
   - Ticket backlog to valid JSON string export.
   - Ticket backlog to formatted Markdown export with schedule and traceability.

---

## Assumptions

1. **Velocity Heuristic:** Story point estimation and duration scheduling assume a baseline team velocity of 10 SP per 14 calendar days.
2. **Calendar Day Scheduling:** Dependency start dates begin on the immediate next calendar day after prerequisite completion. Weekend and holiday calendar exceptions are omitted in this heuristic model.
3. **Single-User Browser Context:** `localStorage` persistence and in-memory API key handling are assumed sufficient for the scope of an internal PM evaluation tool.
4. **AI Role:** Story point values and dependency associations generated by Gemini are treated as initial planning recommendations that must be verified by engineering leads.

---

## Shortcuts / Out of Scope

To ensure high craft, rock-solid tests, and strict adherence to the two assigned problem statements (PS7 & PS10), the following capabilities were deliberately kept out of scope:
- **No Jira / Linear / GitHub API sync:** Exports are produced as downloadable `.json` and `.md` files rather than live bi-directional syncing with third-party trackers.
- **No Multi-User Authentication:** No user accounts, roles, or organization permissions.
- **No Database Backend:** Avoided backend database complexity in favor of client-side modular TypeScript and localStorage.
- **No Rich-Text WYSIWYG Editor:** PRD sections are rendered as structured readable lists and text blocks rather than editable rich-text canvas blocks.
- **No Live Capacity Planning:** Timeline uses the defined deterministic heuristic rather than querying engineer availability or sprint calendars.

---

## Known Limitations

- **Client-Side API Key:** The Gemini API key must be provided in the UI banner during the session. It is stored in memory and cleared upon page reload.
- **LLM Token Limits:** Very large prototype text inputs are constrained by model context and output limits (configured to 8,192 tokens max output).
- **Browser-Scoped Storage:** Projects and tickets saved in `localStorage` are specific to the user's browser and machine.

---

## What I Would Improve With More Time

If extending this into a production SaaS product, the roadmap would prioritize:

1. **Direct Jira & Linear Two-Way Sync:** One-click push of generated tickets directly into Jira or Linear backlogs, complete with epic associations and dependency links.
2. **Team Collaboration & RBAC:** Multi-player PRD editing, commenting, and role-based sign-off workflows (PM, Engineering Lead, Design Lead).
3. **Engineering Capacity & Sprint Calendars:** Upgrade the scheduling engine to support team velocity adjustments, sprint cycle boundaries, non-working days, and assignee allocation.
4. **Multi-Modal Prototype Ingestion:** Support uploading Figma links, wireframe screenshots, or whiteboard sketches directly into the PRD generator using multimodal Gemini vision.
5. **AI Evaluation & Quality Scoring:** Automated ambiguity detection that flags vague requirements or unaddressed edge cases in the PRD before PM approval.

---

## Security / API Key Handling

- **Zero Persistence:** The Gemini API key is never saved to `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, cookies, or remote databases.
- **In-Memory Closure:** The key is maintained solely inside a private module variable in `sessionStore.ts`.
- **Client-Direct Communication:** All API calls are dispatched directly from the client's browser to `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com`. No intermediate proxy servers log or capture API keys.
- **No Repository Secrets:** No API keys are hardcoded or committed to version control.

# Corporate Ownership & AML Investigator

An interactive full-stack graph application designed to investigate multi-hop corporate structures, ultimate beneficial owners (UBO), circular ownership networks, and shared nominee director risks. Backed by **CognoDB** (using OpenCypher via the Bolt protocol) and built with **FastAPI** (Python) and **Next.js** (App Router, Tailwind CSS, and React Force Graph).

---

## Why a Graph Database?

Relational databases (RDBMS) struggle with the variable-length traversals and complex topology analysis required in modern Anti-Money Laundering (AML) investigations.

1. **Exponentially Slow Joins**: Identifying an Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) who controls an operating company through 4–5 hops of holding companies requires multiple self-joins or recursive Common Table Expressions (CTEs). As data grows, query performance degrades exponentially.
2. **Relational Nightmares for Cycles**: Finding circular ownership structures (e.g., Company A owns Company B -> owns Company C -> owns Company A) is extremely difficult to express in SQL, requiring complex recursion and loop-breaking logic. In Cypher, it is a single line: `(c:Company)-[:OWNS*2..6]->(c)`.
3. **Dynamic Schema & Heterogeneous Paths**: Graph databases allow entities (Persons, Companies, Jurisdictions) and their relationships (OWNS, DIRECTOR_OF, LOCATED_IN) to have unique properties (percentages, shares, appointment dates) and traverse them dynamically without rigid schema joins.
4. **Shortest Path Analysis**: Uncovering covert connections between two seemingly unrelated entities is a native, optimized traversal algorithm in graph databases (`shortestPath`), whereas in SQL it requires computing all combinations of paths.

---

## Data Model & Schema

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Person {
        +String id
        +String name
        +String nationality
        +Boolean is_pep
        +Float net_worth
    }
    class Company {
        +String id
        +String name
        +String country
        +String jurisdiction
        +String incorporation_date
        +Float risk_score
    }
    class Jurisdiction {
        +String code
        +String name
        +Boolean is_tax_haven
    }

    Person --> Company : OWNS {percentage: Float, shares: Int}
    Company --> Company : OWNS {percentage: Float, shares: Int}
    Person --> Company : DIRECTOR_OF {appointed_date: String}
    Company --> Jurisdiction : LOCATED_IN
```

### Nodes
- **`Company`**: Represents corporate entities. Includes attributes such as `risk_score` (representing AML risk) and corporate jurisdiction.
- **`Person`**: Represents human individuals. Includes attributes for Politically Exposed Person (`is_pep`) status and net worth.
- **`Jurisdiction`**: Represents countries or sovereign jurisdictions, detailing whether they are tax havens.

### Relationships
- **`OWNS`**: Links a `Person` or a `Company` to another `Company` with properties `percentage` (float representation of ownership percentage) and `shares` (integer).
- **`DIRECTOR_OF`**: Links a `Person` to a `Company` with the `appointed_date` string.
- **`LOCATED_IN`**: Links a `Company` to its incorporating `Jurisdiction`.

---

## CognoDB Setup Guide

CognoDB is a managed graph database service. It is fully compatible with the official Neo4j Bolt driver and supports standard OpenCypher queries.

1. **Instance Creation**:
   - Access the CognoDB console.
   - Deploy a new graph database instance.
   - Choose OpenCypher / Neo4j compatible mode.
2. **Credentials Extraction**:
   - Save the Bolt connection URL (`bolt+s://...`).
   - Extract the auto-generated password.
   - Set the default username to `cognodb` (unless configured otherwise).
3. **Environment Setup**:
   - Copy `.env.example` to `.env` in the root folder.
   - Replace the placeholders with your connection details:
     ```env
     COGNODB_URI=bolt+s://your-instance-domain.cogno.db:7687
     COGNODB_USER=cognodb
     COGNODB_PASSWORD=your-secret-password
     ```

---

## Core Cypher Queries Breakdown

### 1. Ultimate Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Detection
Finds all human owners (`Person`) who control a company directly or indirectly across 1 to 5 hops of ownership:
```cypher
MATCH path = (p:Person)-[:OWNS*1..5]->(target:Company {id: $companyId})
RETURN p, path, length(path) as depth
```
* **Breakdown**: Traverses the `OWNS` edge from a human node (`Person`) through any intermediate corporate nodes to the target company, calculating path length.

### 2. Circular Ownership Loop Detection
Discovers complex holding networks where a company owns part of itself through a loop of other companies:
```cypher
MATCH path = (c:Company {id: $companyId})-[:OWNS*2..6]->(c)
RETURN path
```
* **Breakdown**: Starts at a specific company, follows the `OWNS` relationship across 2 to 6 hops, and terminates back at the starting company node.

### 3. Shared Intermediaries & Directorship Networks
Identifies nominee directors managing multiple legal entities, which is a common red flag for shell companies:
```cypher
MATCH (p:Person)-[:DIRECTOR_OF]->(c1:Company), (p)-[:DIRECTOR_OF]->(c2:Company)
WHERE c1.id <> c2.id
RETURN p, c1, c2
```
* **Breakdown**: Matches any individual who serves as a director for two distinct company nodes, returning the shared individual and the linked companies.

### 4. Shortest Path Covert Connections
Finds the shortest network path (up to 10 connections deep) between two arbitrary entities:
```cypher
MATCH path = shortestPath((start)-[*1..10]-(end))
WHERE start.id = $startId AND end.id = $endId
RETURN path
```
* **Breakdown**: Uses the native graph `shortestPath` function to find any connection (regardless of relationship type or direction) between a start and target node.

---

## Local Setup & Run Commands

### Prerequisites
- Python 3.10+
- Node.js 18+
- npm or yarn

### 1. Setup Backend & Seed Database
```bash
# Navigate to backend
cd backend

# Create virtual environment
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate

# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Run seed script (from the root directory, with activated venv)
cd ..
python scripts/seed.py

# Run backend server (from backend directory)
cd backend
uvicorn main:app --reload --port 8000
```

### 2. Setup Frontend
```bash
# Navigate to frontend
cd frontend

# Install dependencies
npm install

# Run dev server
npm run dev
```
Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) to access the interactive investigator UI.

# Visual AI Agent

A production-ready, high-performance Visual AI Agent built as a Chrome Extension (Manifest V3) backed by a Node.js + Express + Prisma + PostgreSQL backend.

---

## Key Features

- **Manifest V3 Architecture**: Modular background Service Worker, Content Scripts, and React + Tailwind Popup UI.
- **Privacy-First Informed Monitoring**: Captures visible portion of active tab (`chrome.tabs.captureVisibleTab()`) with explicit user consent toggles and graceful handling of unsupported pages (`chrome://`, Web Store).
- **Two-Tier Frame Deduplication**: Fast 32-bit FNV-1a pixel checksum comparison drops identical captures instantly to minimize CPU and memory overhead.
- **Binary Offline Queue**: Stores captured screenshots as `Blob` / `ArrayBuffer` objects directly inside IndexedDB, avoiding the ~33% Base64 overhead.
- **Normalized Event Pipeline**: Throttles (200ms) and deduplicates high-frequency DOM events (`click`, `keypress`, `scroll`, `resize`, `focus`, `blur`) with sensitive data masking.
- **Exponential Backoff Ingestion**: API client handles network failures with retry queues.
- **Pragmatic Backend Architecture**: Clean 3-layer `Controller → Service → Prisma Client → PostgreSQL` design with full Swagger OpenAPI docs at `/api-docs`.
- **Health Check Endpoint**: `GET /api/v1/health` providing database status, queue depth, uptime, Node version, and memory telemetry.
- **DevOps & CI/CD**: Docker Compose production stack and GitHub Actions CI workflow (ESLint, Prettier, TypeScript checks, Vitest unit tests, dependency audit).

# Longest Valid Parentheses

## Approach

The solution uses a stack to store indices of unmatched parentheses.

1. Initialize the stack with -1.
2. Push indices of '('.
3. For ')':
   - Pop one index.
   - If the stack becomes empty, push the current index.
   - Otherwise, calculate the current valid substring length.

## Complexity

Time: O(n)
Space: O(n)

# Resume-JD Matcher (Senior-Level Implementation)

A high-performance Node.js REST API designed to parse PDF résumés and match them against multiple Job Descriptions (JDs) using rule-based parsing and optimized matching algorithms.

## 🚀 Key Features

- **Set-Based Matching (O(1))**: Optimized skill lookup using `Set` data structures instead of `Array.includes`, significantly reducing time complexity for large résumés.
- **Startup JD Caching**: Job Descriptions are parsed exactly once during server initialization. This eliminates redundant file I/O and text processing, ensuring sub-millisecond match times.
- **Intelligent Extraction**:
  - **Experience**: Handles both direct mentions (e.g., "5+ years") and date-range calculations (e.g., "Jan 2020 – Present").
  - **Salary**: Regex-based extraction for LPA (Indian), INR (₹), and USD ($) formats.
- **RESTful API**: Clean endpoint structure with health monitoring and skill discovery.
- **Memory Storage**: Uses Multer `memoryStorage` to process PDFs directly from buffers, ensuring no temporary files are written to disk.

## 📁 System Architecture

```text
/src
 ├── controllers/
 │     └── match.controller.js  # Pipeline orchestration & result sorting
 ├── services/
 │     ├── resume.parser.js      # PDF extraction & data synthesis
 │     ├── jd.parser.js          # Pre-caching JD skills
 │     ├── skill.matcher.js      # Optimized skill intersection
 │     └── score.calculator.js   # Accuracy score computation
```

🏋️ AI Fitness Coach App

An advanced, full-stack fitness assistant built on Next.js, powered by Google's Gemini LLM and Imagen 3.0 for personalized workout plans, diet regimes, and visual guidance. The application includes user authentication and persistent plan storage using Firebase Firestore.

✨ Features

Personalized Plan Generation: Users input their goals, fitness levels, diet, and equipment (Home/Gym) to generate completely custom 7-day workout plans and daily diet breakdowns using Gemini.

Persistent Storage: Generated plans are securely saved and loaded for authenticated users using Firebase Firestore.

Visual Aid (AI Image Generation): Clicking on any exercise or meal generates a realistic, high-quality image of the exercise form or the food using Imagen 3.0.

Voice Features: Option to play back the workout and diet plans using the browser's Text-to-Speech (TTS) API.

Daily Motivation: Fetches a fresh, AI-generated motivational quote daily.

Responsive UI: Built with Tailwind CSS and Shadcn UI for a smooth, modern, and adaptive experience on all devices.

Theme Toggle: Supports Dark and Light mode.

💻 Tech Stack

The application is built on a robust, full-stack architecture leveraging the following key technologies:

Frontend: Next.js (App Router), React, TypeScript.

Purpose: Full-stack framework, routing, and component architecture.

Styling & UI: Tailwind CSS, Shadcn UI.

Purpose: Utility-first styling and robust, accessible UI components.

Generative AI (LLM): Gemini.

Purpose: Generating structured Workout, Diet, and Motivational Plans.

Image AI: Imagen 3.0 (via Canvas API).

Purpose: Visualizing exercises and meals on demand.

Database: Firebase Firestore.

Purpose: Secure, real-time storage for user data and saved plans.

Authentication: Firebase Auth (Custom Token).

Purpose: Authentication management for persistent user sessions.

⚙️ Setup and Installation

Follow these steps to get a copy of the project running on your local machine.

Prerequisites

Node.js (version 18 or later)

npm

A Gemini API Key (from Google AI Studio or Google Cloud)

A Firebase Project (or access to the Canvas environment)

Step 1: Clone and Install

# Clone the repository
git clone [YOUR_REPO_URL] ai-fitness-coach-app
cd ai-fitness-coach-app

# Install all dependencies (Next.js, Firebase, Gen AI, UI libs)
npm install


Step 2: Configure Environment Variables

Create a file named .env.local in the root of your project directory (ai-fitness-coach-app/) and add your API key.

# .env.local

# Your Gemini API Key for server-side use in API Routes
GEMINI_API_KEY="YOUR_GEMINI_API_KEY_HERE"

# NOTE: Firebase configuration is handled automatically by the Canvas environment.
# If running locally, you must provide the firebaseConfig JSON string here.
# __firebase_config='{...}'


Step 3: Run the Development Server

Start the application using the Next.js development script:

npm run dev


The application will be accessible at http://localhost:3000.

📌 Development Notes

API Endpoints

/api/generate-plan (POST): Calls Gemini to generate the structured plan based on user input.

/api/daily-quote (GET): Fetches a new motivational quote from Gemini.

Firestore Structure

The application uses the security rules defined in the Canvas environment, storing data under:

/artifacts/{appId}/users/{userId}/plans/{planId}

Plans are stored with metadata (name, goal, level) and the full AI-generated plan object is serialized as a JSON string in the document.

# Fullstack Auth Demo

This repository contains a minimal, working full-stack authentication demo built for learning and rapid prototyping.

- Backend: Node.js + Express
- Frontend: React (simple static demo in `public/` for quick start)
- Auth: bcryptjs for password hashing + JWT for session tokens
- Data store: `data/users.json` (file-backed JSON store — demo only)

This README documents setup, development workflows, security considerations, and recommended next steps to harden and expand the project.

## Quick start (run the demo locally)

1. Copy the example env and set a secret:

```powershell
copy .env.example .env
# Edit .env and set JWT_SECRET
```

2. Install dependencies and start the server:

```powershell
npm install
npm start
```

3. Open the demo in your browser:

http://localhost:3000

4. Run the automated tests (end-to-end smoke tests):

```powershell
npm test
```

## Project layout

- `index.js` — Express app and API endpoints. The app is exported for testability; running `node index.js` starts the server.
- `public/` — static frontend (quick demo using React + CDN in-browser Babel). Replace with a proper React app for production.
- `data/users.json` — demo-only JSON user store (reset by tests).
- `__tests__/` — Jest + Supertest end-to-end tests for the auth flow.

## API (summary)

- POST `/api/signup` — body: `{ username, password }` — creates user, returns `{ message, token }` on success
- POST `/api/signin` — body: `{ username, password }` — returns `{ message, token }` on success
- GET `/api/me` — protected; requires header `Authorization: Bearer <token>` — returns user profile

Responses use JSON with meaningful HTTP status codes (400 for bad input, 401 for auth issues, 409 for conflicts).

## Development notes

- The Express app is exported from `index.js` so tests can import it directly without starting a network server.
- The frontend in `public/` is intentionally minimal for fast iteration. Recommended migration: use Vite or Create React App (see next section).

## Recommended polish & migration steps

Below are concrete steps (small → medium → larger) you can follow to finalize this project for production readiness.

1. Frontend modularization (recommended)

a. Create a separate modern React app (Vite recommended) in `frontend/` (TypeScript optional):

```powershell
npm create vite@latest frontend -- --template react
cd frontend
npm install
```

b. Move the `public/app.jsx`, `styles.css` components into React components; create small reusable components: `Input`, `Button`, `Form`, `ErrorMessage`, `Loader`.

c. Use CSS Modules or styled-components for modular styles. Enable ESLint + Prettier.

d. Configure the frontend to call backend API via a relative proxy in dev (Vite `proxy` or CRA `proxy` setting) or provide an environment variable `VITE_API_URL`.

2. Backend persistence (replace JSON file)

Options (choose one):

- SQLite (local, easy to adopt) with an ORM/Query builder: Prisma or Knex
- PostgreSQL (recommended for production)
- MongoDB (if you prefer document store + Mongoose)

Example quick migration with SQLite + Prisma:

```powershell
npm install prisma --save-dev
npx prisma init --datasource-provider sqlite
# define User model in prisma/schema.prisma and run `npx prisma migrate dev`
```

Implement database-backed user model, and replace `readUsers` / `writeUsers` with DB queries. Keep password hashing with bcrypt.

3. Security hardening

- Store `JWT_SECRET` and any credentials in environment variables (already supported via `.env`). Never commit secrets.
- Use HTTPS in production. For local dev, generate dev certs via `mkcert` and run your server with HTTPS (or use a reverse proxy).
- Prefer storing tokens in httpOnly, Secure cookies (for browser apps) instead of localStorage to reduce XSS risk. Use CSRF protections for cookie-based auth (double-submit cookie / same-site cookies).
- Implement refresh tokens (rotate refresh tokens, short-lived access tokens).
- Enforce strong password rules and rate-limit authentication endpoints (express-rate-limit).
- Sanitize inputs and use helmet middleware for secure headers:

```js
const helmet = require("helmet");
app.use(helmet());
```

4. Testing & CI

- Keep the existing Jest + Supertest tests. Add unit tests for utility functions and additional integration tests (DB migrations, token expiry).
- Add coverage reporting via `--coverage` and fail build on low coverage thresholds.
- Add a GitHub Actions workflow to run `npm ci`, `npm test`, and optionally build the frontend.

Example minimal GitHub Actions snippet (.github/workflows/ci.yml):

```yaml
name: CI
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 18
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test --if-present
```

5. UI/UX polish & accessibility

- Ensure form controls have labels and ARIA attributes where needed (the demo provides labels already).
- Add keyboard focus states, visible contrast, and test with a screen reader.
- Improve responsiveness across breakpoints; add small animations for feedback and an accessible color theme.

6. Feature expansion ideas

- Password reset (email token flow)
- OAuth sign-in (Google, GitHub) via Passport.js or OAuth libraries
- User profiles and role-based access control (RBAC)
- Admin panel with user management
- Account locking + rate limiting for brute-force protection

## Testing details

- End-to-end tests are in `__tests__/auth.e2e.test.js` (Supertest + Jest). They run against the exported Express app for fast, reliable tests.
- To run tests locally:

```powershell
npm test
```

## Security checklist before production

- Replace JSON store with a hardened DB and parameterized queries / ORM.
- Ensure HTTPS and secure cookie handling.
- Use long, random JWT secrets and rotate them if needed.
- Implement logging and monitoring for auth failures.
- Add automated vulnerability scanning and dependency updates.

## Troubleshooting

- If `npm start` says port in use, change `PORT` in `.env`.
- If tests fail due to leftover users, remove or reset `data/users.json` to `[]`.

## Contribution & development

If you'd like to help polish this project, follow these steps:

1. Create a branch for your change.
2. Implement small, testable improvements (migrations, frontend modularization, additional tests).
3. Add/update tests and run `npm test` locally before opening a PR.

---

If you want, I can now:

- Scaffold a proper `frontend/` app using Vite + React (with TypeScript if you prefer) and wire it to this backend.
- Replace the JSON storage with SQLite + Prisma (quick local DB) and update tests accordingly.
- Add the GitHub Actions CI workflow and sample environment configuration.

Tell me which of the above you'd like implemented and I'll proceed with concrete edits and tests.

## Vercel deployment (quick)

If you want public frontend and backend URLs quickly, Vercel is the fastest path. Below are two simple options — a single-project approach which serves the static frontend from `public/` and the Express app as serverless functions under `/api/*` (recommended), and an alternative using two separate projects (one for frontend, one for backend).

Prerequisites
- Push this repository to a Git provider (GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket).
- Have a Vercel account. Optionally install the Vercel CLI (`npm i -g vercel`).

Single-project (recommended)

1. Ensure `vercel.json` and `api/index.js` are present (they are included in this repo). The default layout this repo uses expects static files in `public/` and serverless functions under `api/`.
2. Import the repository into Vercel via the Vercel dashboard: https://vercel.com/new — select your repo and follow the UI. Vercel will detect the `api/` folder and treat functions under it as serverless endpoints.
3. Set required environment variables in the Vercel project settings (Settings → Environment Variables):
   - `JWT_SECRET` — the JWT signing secret used by the backend.
   - `OPENAI_API_KEY` — (optional) your OpenAI API key if you want real LLM responses. If absent, the demo uses a mock echo fallback.
4. (Optional) If you instead build a modern frontend in `frontend/` (Vite/CRA), set the Build Command to `npm run build` and Output Directory to `frontend/dist` (or the location your build generates). If you keep the simple static `public/` folder in this repo, Vercel will serve it as static assets automatically.
5. Deploy and open the project URL shown by Vercel. Your backend endpoints will be available under the same domain at `/api/*` (for example: `https://<your-project>.vercel.app/api/llm`).

Two-project alternative (frontend + backend separated)

Use this option if you prefer independent lifecycle and domains for front- and back-end.

Backend (serverless functions)
- Create a new Vercel project and import the repository, but configure the Root Directory to the repository root. The `api/` folder will be used for serverless functions.
- Set the same environment variables (`JWT_SECRET`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`) in the backend project settings.

Frontend (static site)
- Create another Vercel project that points to the same repo but set the Root Directory to `public/` or to your `frontend/` build output (e.g., `frontend/dist` if you use Vite). This project will serve the static frontend only.
- If your frontend calls the backend at runtime, set an environment variable in the frontend project for the backend base URL (for example `VITE_API_BASE=https://<backend-project>.vercel.app/api`). Replace in your frontend config as needed.

Quick CLI deploy (optional)

If you prefer the CLI, these commands work in PowerShell (after installing `vercel` and logging in):

```powershell
npm i -g vercel
vercel login
# From the repo root:
vercel --prod
```

To add environment variables with the CLI:

```powershell
vercel env add OPENAI_API_KEY production
vercel env add JWT_SECRET production
```

Verification
- Frontend: open the Vercel project URL in your browser (root of the deployment).
- Backend: visit `https://<your-project>.vercel.app/api/me` (requires Authorization header) or `https://<your-project>.vercel.app/api/` to confirm the functions are reachable. Example API endpoints:
  - POST `/api/signup`
  - POST `/api/signin`
  - POST `/api/llm`

Notes & tips
- If you want live OpenAI responses, set `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the Vercel project. Without it, the demo uses a local mock echo so you can still exercise the UI.
- Vercel serverless functions have cold starts and execution time limits — for production workloads you may prefer a dedicated server or managed container (Heroku, Railway, Render, AWS ECS/EKS, etc.).
- If your frontend needs a build step (Vite), push the `frontend/` app and set the build command and output directory in the Vercel import settings.

If you'd like, I can produce the exact sequence of CLI commands (and any small edits) to deploy this repo to Vercel and then return the public frontend + backend URLs. Tell me which option you prefer (single-project or two-project) and whether you want me to produce the `vercel` CLI commands for your environment.
